question.text: 'Vikramaditya AIF' is being incorporated as a Company (Section 8 style) under the Companies Act 2013 — the least preferred route. Which of the following is a MAJOR constraint of the Company structure that makes it inferior to trust/LLP?

answer.text: Companies cannot issue units, only equity shares, making unit-class waterfalls impossible
Companies cannot offer limited liability to investors
Companies cannot appoint an investment manager
Companies are restricted to a maximum of 200 investors under private placement rules, vs 1000 permitted for an AIF scheme

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 8.4 Alternative 3: companies face a 200-investor cap under private placement rules (Section 42), whereas AIF regulations permit 1000 investors per scheme (accredited investors excluded). This is a binding structural limit. **The Trap:** Option A — companies can issue equity with differential rights, so waterfalls are possible but clunky. Option C is false. Option D is false — companies offer limited liability. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the 200 vs 1000 investor-cap mismatch explicitly; XIX-A/B do not go into this granularity. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** If an LP tells you 'we only invest in Section 8 Company AIFs for governance comfort', push back: the 200-investor cap collides with your 1000 target, and you will hit it mid-fundraise.
